title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 15 — QA round 4's ref-accuracy findings, scored per RUNNER rule 6 (a pin scores only the layer it drives)
body:
Refs #24579
Clause-②: no

Round 15 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor (claim `6290925424`, PM loop round 25). It applies the "Checklist-accuracy findings / fixture gaps" section of QA round 4's Tier 1 record (#24840, framework `307ce4c4`) under RUNNER rule 6, "A pin scores only the layer it drives" (`RUNNER.md` rule 6, landed by PR #24811), and round 6's theme-B rule (PR #24697).

Only checklist text changes. 21 items in 9 area files each take one `revision` bump and one `history` row, and each row names #24840 and the finding. There is no product code, test, pin, changeset text or `RUNNER.md` change. `records-forms.record-discussion-mentions` is untouched.

- Base `b1676441ba`, which is PR #24869's merge commit. `origin/main` `98c3d00447` is merged in `c4da0e622b` and touches no `docs/qa/**` path.
- Every item and every pin named below was re-read at the base before it was written. Rounds 12 to 14 edited several of these items after #24840's base, and the items they settled are listed under "Items left alone".
- A scripted span editor made every edit. It never re-serialises a file. For each area file it re-parses the result and asserts four things: the new document equals the old one with the declared ops applied; every other item and top-level key is value-equal; each edited item's changed paths are inside its declared fields plus `revision` and the one new history row; and the text outside the edited items is byte-identical. A whole-branch check against the base agrees: 21 items changed, each with revision +1 and exactly one appended row.
- The new history rows carry the placeholder ref `#PENDING-24579R15`, because a row's `ref` names this PR and the PR had no number yet. The next commit on this branch swaps in this PR's number and changes nothing else.

## How rule 6 was applied

- A pin scores a clause only when it drives the layer the clause's oracle sits at: unit, driver, engine, HTTP door, boot log or CLI exit. The layer is read off the pin's own harness, never off its file name.
- A ref that claims more is narrowed per clause (theme-B). Where no pin holds a full clause, `automated` is removed and a `fixtures.knownGaps` line says what the pin does assert and when `automated` may return. That happened on 6 items.
- Item text that told a runner to score an api or log clause from a lower pin ("Unit fallback", "score from the pin", "unit-pin verdict") now cites that pin as evidence of its own layer only. Where the live leg cannot be staged on stock, the clause is recorded `blocked(fixture)` with the pin beside it. It is never scored pass.
- Negatives are read the same way. A negative whose FAIL condition is a door's answer (a 2xx, an envelope, a row the door left) is scored at that door. A negative whose FAIL condition is a state the pin's own layer owns and reads directly (a spawn the provider never reaches, a DDL change the driver's sync makes, a background task that throws) can be scored at that layer. Three QA round 4 verdicts read differently under this rule, and they are listed under "Items left alone".
- A missing pin was added only after reading that it asserts the named clause's whole oracle at that clause's layer. Where it asserts half, the item says which half instead.

### The defective pin, for the PM to file

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-drift.test.ts`, the case "is force-disabled under NODE_ENV=production (warns, does not alter)", stages `relax_not_null`. ADR-0113 made that op `needs_confirm`, and a safe reconcile applies only `safe` ops. So the column stays NOT NULL with or without the production branch of `reconcileAndWarnDrift` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`). The sibling case "does NOT auto-relax a stray NOT NULL — needs_confirm survives dev auto-reconcile" asserts the same outcome with no `NODE_ENV` set. The case also asserts no warning. #24840 names the repair: stage `replace_unique_index` and assert the warning. This PR does not touch the test. The ledger now scores nothing from that case and records it in the item's `knownGaps[2]`.

## Items left alone, with reasons

Round 14 (PR #24857) removed the stale marker, and the ref claims acceptance[1] from objectui `saved-view-filter.spec.ts` (blob `94a201c63a0a` at `616df6598b42`). That spec opens the shipped `in_progress` view on the live stack, asserts the count bar reads 2, and asserts that no data request was refused. A rule-array filter is refused 400, so the green is the AST filter being accepted.
- `records-forms.related-list-server-pagination` ("its only pin is stale"): no longer holds. Round 14 removed the stale marker after reading the repaired spec, and the ref claims acceptance[2] only.

- `approvals.decision-action-matrix` negative[1]: not added. The service pin throws THROTTLED and the route pin maps a mocked rejection to 429, but neither drives the remind door. "A silent second success" is that door's answer.
- `identity-auth.admin-lifecycle-operations` acceptance[5]: the added case is its exemption half. Its refusal half stays partly by hand, because `admin-platform-admin-standing.dogfood.test.ts` re-reads the target `sys_user` but never the rows that user owns.

- `integration-system.datasource-admin-lifecycle`: only respelled, as #24840 asked. Its ref's scope ("pins route behavior + envelope") is not narrowed per clause.
- `platform-core.metadata-authoring-roundtrip` keeps `automated.kind` "api", although its remaining full-clause pin is an objectui live spec. `kind` is free text that no gate reads.
- QA round 4 verdicts this round reads differently. The record scored them pass from lower pins: `encrypted-field-behavior` acceptance[3] and negative[1] (engine), `settings-audit-secret-fingerprint` negative[0]–[1] (rows on stub sinks), and `approvals.decision-action-matrix` negative[1] (service). Under the rule above, each is now evidence beside a hand-driven or `blocked(fixture)` verdict.

1. "Rounds 12–14 already settled list-view-capabilities, related-list-server-pagination and field-accept-maxsize's a3." This holds for the first two. It does not hold for the third: round 12's case is handler-direct, so the item's ref still scores no clause, and the finding was applied.
2. "Most bare-ref rows narrow rather than drop." This holds 3 of 4. connector-stdio, dataset-report and protocol-18 narrow. webhook-lifecycle drops, because its one pin holds only half of acceptance[0].

The verify now says so, because the rewritten knownGap would otherwise contradict it.

## Gates

The derived list is `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, computed on the actual change set: 9 paths against merge base `98c3d0044`, at head `c4da0e622b`. It gives 13 commands. Each one ran at that head with its exit code captured before any pipe, and each exited 0:

`node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --self-test` · `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs` · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` · `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `pnpm check:doc-authoring` · `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` · `pnpm check:gitlink-declared` · `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `pnpm check:platform-checklist` · `pnpm check:refd-timer-probe` · `pnpm check:watch-hint-literal`

Both were built under the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`), and the rerun exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".
